To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(i) the application of a quantitative approach to paleoclimatic interpretation of isotope data from biogenic hardparts can be used to derive estimates of mean annual temperature, and of seasonal temperature range, from data sets with incomplete coverage of annual isotope cycles; (ii) the method is applicable to a wide variety of data sets, including those that have been published in the literature; (iii) the method is particularly useful for interpreting data from systems that exhibit a high degree of seasonality,

(1) the application of a computational approach to stable isotopic data from biogenic hardparts yields robust estimates of both mean annual and seasonal variations in δ18O and/or temperature, and (2) these estimates are not biased by the presence of noise in the data, by the presence or absence of extreme values, or by the presence or lack of a full seasonal cycle.
